## READ THIS FRONT PAGE EVERY SINGLE TIME YOU HEAR THE WORD VAMILY
Not once. Every time. Rules change on this page and nowhere else, so a chat that
remembers last week's rules is wrong. Paolo never pastes anything; he types the
one word, and this page is the briefing.

0. VAMILY is a keyword. It has nothing to do with families or dynasties. It means:
   read this page, find your section below, do your job from it.
1. Paolo talks ONLY to the coordinator (folded to one line 10/16 by rule 96: no lane named it for 33 sweeps; the full text is records/BOHEMIA_EVAPORATED_10_16_26.md).
2. FIND YOUR SECTION by this chat's number and name (the list is right below). A
   fresh chat with no name takes the first line marked UNCLAIMED, writes CLAIMED on
   it, commits, and that is its role for life. AS OF 9/14: the one UNCLAIMED line is
   20 PORTRAIT (Paolo 9/14: "we might need to open up a new chat for the portrait");
   PLUMBER is claimed. AS OF 9/20 THERE ARE NO UNCLAIMED LINES: 20 PORTRAIT is CLAIMED
   (session portrait-vamily-yke55s, Paolo opened the chat 9/20). A brand-new chat with
   no name asks the coordinator instead of taking a line.
3. READ YOUR SECTION'S MODE AND STATE LINES FIRST. STATE says what is built, what
   is not, and what nobody has checked, so you know what you do not know.
4. Every job carries a TWO-WORD label in [brackets], for him (folded to one line 10/16 by rule 96: no lane named it for 33 sweeps; the full text is records/BOHEMIA_EVAPORATED_10_16_26.md).
5. IF YOU ALREADY HOLD A CLAIMED JOB, VAMILY MEANS CONTINUE IT, from where your
   handoff block says you stopped. A job takes as many rounds as it takes; nobody
   expects one round. Otherwise take the FIRST line marked OPEN in your section,
   change it to CLAIMED <date> <session>, commit and push BEFORE you start.
6. MODE: BUILD means build it, prove it on the real surface (the walked city and
   the demo, on a phone if you can), re-cut the demo, run your lane's gates, then
   change the line to SHIPPED <date> <commit> and push. Mark SHIPPED only when the
   job's own ship test is met; a half-done job marked SHIPPED is worse than an open
   one, never rush to close a line.
   MODE: RESEARCH means DO NOT IMPLEMENT: one research round on the question (the records call it a "day"; it is one VAMILY, not a calendar day, and you never call it a day to Paolo), both
   angles (the best games ever made, and the real world), one finding that proves
   us wrong, measured against our repo, a written record, test material tagged
   draft:true in a bank file never in the game, a ROUTED section; mark SHIPPED
   with the record path.
   MODE: PARKED means nobody touches it until Paolo reopens it.
7. Every mechanic is 120 BPM friendly or it is not done. A row is not shipped
   until it is in the walked surface AND the demo.
8. STANDING DUTIES, every round: VAMILY first; play it before you call it shipped;
   his bugs beat your queue; run your gates, never ship red; rewrite your handoff
   block before you end. ADDED 9/13: if your diff touches engine/, rebuild the two
   derived slices (the RUN_CURRENT slice and the demo) in the same commit; PLUMBER

*** ROUND 5, 9/18 -- THE WALK NUMBER WAS NOT A FRAME RATE. IT WAS A PLAYER PRESSED AGAINST A WALL. (PLUMBER, row [sixty fps]. Record: records/BOHEMIA_THE_WALK_WAS_A_PLAYER_STUCK_AGAINST_A_WALL_9_18_26.md) ***
 LAST ROUND LEFT TWO BUDGETS OUT OF THE CLAMP because the record and the gate disagreed about the same metric by 6.3x (8.8 fps against 55.8) and 2.5x. Reconciling them was the named next line. Both are now closed and the cause was one bug in this lane's own instrument.
 REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, one boot each, everything else identical: skipFirstMinute=true gives a settled walk of 60.0 fps over 110 cells; skipFirstMinute=false gives 8.8 fps over THREE CELLS. 8.8 is the record's number exactly. THE CAUSE: every walk in the instrument pressed the same direction, including the settled one that runs AFTER a sixty-second first-minute walk the same way. So the settled sample measured a player who had been walking north for over a minute and was against something. IT WAS NEVER A FRAME RATE: the good-bursts rate was 60.2 in BOTH runs. The game drew at sixty the whole time; one player was walking and the other was stuck.
 THE VALIDITY FLOOR WAS TOO WEAK TO CATCH IT. The instrument already said "a sample that did not move is not a slow sample, it is a broken one" and the rule was right; the THRESHOLD asked "did he move at all" and one cell passed. Measured: a walking player covers 110-123 cells in 6 s, a stuck one covers 3. The floor is now TWO CELLS PER SECOND OF HOLD, ten times under a healthy walk and four times over a stuck one, and an invalid sample carries WHY in its own body.
 FIXED AND MEASURED BOTH WAYS: before 60.0 fps/110 cells against 8.8 fps/3 cells; after 58.3/110 against 50.9/110. A 6.3x disagreement became 1.15x. In the refreshed record the walk reads 57.1 fps against the gate's live 60.4, and main thread 20.6% against 17.9% -- SAME ROOT CAUSE, no separate hunt needed, because a player against a wall barely draws so his frame rate and his thread cost both read low.
 SO BOTH LINES ARE BACK IN THE CLAMP and notClampedOnPurpose is now EMPTY. Six budget lines clamped instead of four: fight 10->47.81, walking 6->40.77, main thread 56->33, beats missed 9->4, alpha walk 6->41.66, alpha beats 11->4. Every held line sits between 1.15x and 1.60x of what the build does, against a guard that fails anything over 2x. Excluding them last round with their numbers written down was the right call while they disagreed and the wrong thing to keep once they did not.
 THE GATE IS 38 PASSED / 3 FAILED (it was 36/3 last round and 32/3 when this row started). ONE LINE FOR RUN, THIRD ROUND RUNNING: all three reds are the same bug, #daycard is inset:0 and sits over all eight direction buttons on boot, so time to first play cannot be measured on either surface.

*** ROUND 4, 9/16 -- THE SPEED GATE WOULD HAVE ACCEPTED A SIX-TIMES REGRESSION IN THE FIGHT, AND NOW IT WILL NOT. (PLUMBER, row [sixty fps]. Record: records/BOHEMIA_A_BUDGET_THAT_ACCEPTS_A_SIX_TIMES_REGRESSION_9_16_26.md) ***
 THE HOLE: the fight budget the gate held was 10 fps while the build delivered 60. A 5.7x regression on the pillar mechanic would have passed green. Last round named this and refused to half-fix it; this round measured what a fix needs.
 THE CAUSE, MEASURED IN TWO PARTS. (1) A history entry carries no build identity, so a sample from a build with a real bug anchors the budget straight across the fix: fightLo went 17.6, 25, 15.4, 15.6, then 54.3 the moment somebody re-measured. (2) THE BIGGER ONE: the 40% spread that justified "worst of six refreshes" was measured on ONE metric and applied to ALL of them. Four passes of one unchanged tree: bytes 0.0%, beats missed 0.0%, THE FIGHT 0.5%, boot blocking 4.2%, walking 4.4%, main thread 8.3%. Bytes literally do not move and the fight varies by half a percent, and they were being given the headroom of a metric that swings 40%.
 THE FIX: keep worst-of-history, then CLAMP each line so it cannot sit further from what the build does today than that metric's OWN measured spread plus a stated margin. The margin is 0.25 and it is grounded, not picked: three times the largest spread on any valid metric across six passes. A floor on my own rule: fewer than three samples is not a spread, so the clamp is skipped and the record says so on its face. MOVED: fightFps 10 -> 47.81, beatMissed 9 -> 3, alphaWalkFps 6 -> 10, alphaBeatMissed 11 -> 4. The live gate now reads the fight at 60 against a budget of 47.7.
 *** THEN MY OWN FIX WENT RED AND I DID NOT WIDEN THE MARGIN TO HIDE IT. *** Clamping main-thread-busy gave budget 9 against a live 15.8. Widening the margin until it went green would have loosened the fight's clamp too, and the fight is the one that needed fixing. So I compared EVERY held line's record value against the gate's own live value on the same tree: fight 60 vs 60 agree, bytes agree exactly, beats 2 vs 2.6 close, MAIN THREAD 6.4% vs 15.8% (2.5x apart), WALKING 8.8 fps vs 55.8 fps (6.3x apart). TWO OF THE LINES THIS GATE HOLDS ARE DERIVED FROM NUMBERS THAT DO NOT DESCRIBE WHAT THE GATE MEASURES. Both keep their old budget; reconciling the two walk samples is its own job and is the next line of this row.
 AND A RED THAT BLINDED THE WHOLE GATE: the record-completeness block ended in a flat abort, so the moment any one line went red the other thirty-odd checks never ran. Measured: a card over the pad made first play unmeasurable and a gate with 37 working checks reported 18 passed / 1 failed and said nothing else. Now it gives up only if the record is structurally unusable. Same verdict, same exit code, but one blocked measurement costs one line instead of the whole page.
 ONE LINE FOR RUN, AND IT HAS GOT WORSE SINCE LAST ROUND: all three remaining reds are the same bug. #daycard is inset:0 and sits over all eight direction buttons on boot. LAST ROUND THE DEMO STILL GOT THROUGH ONCE AT 18,027 ms; THIS ROUND NO PASS ON EITHER SURFACE REACHED A FIRST STEP AT ALL, so time-to-first-play cannot be measured on this build. I let that go red rather than carry the last number that happened to get through. Gate was 32 passed / 3 failed before this round and is 36 / 3 now.

*** ROUND 3, 9/15 -- THE FIGHT RUNS AT SIXTY ON THIS BOX AND AT SEVEN ON A PHONE. (PLUMBER, row [sixty fps]. Record: records/BOHEMIA_THE_FIGHT_IS_SIXTY_HERE_AND_SEVEN_ON_A_PHONE_9_15_26.md) ***
 THE SPEED INSTRUMENT HAS MEASURED A PHONE-SHAPED CPU SINCE 9/5 AND THREW IT AWAY EVERY TIME. It defaults to both 1x and 4x, but the refresh command written in its own record pinned it to --cpu 1. So every speed number this fleet has ever quoted describes a machine several times faster than his phone. FIXED: the refresh no longer pins the throttle, the record now carries a phone-shaped block, and the gate PRINTS it beside the 1x numbers and FAILS if a future record has none.
 ONE REFRESH, TWO REPEATS, ONE WINDOW; the throttle proved real in the same run by the yardstick (31.75 ms at 1x against 136.7 ms at 4x):
   the fight                57.2 fps here   ->    7.1 fps on a phone-shaped CPU (alpha: 60.1 -> 9.4)
   boot blocked the thread  19,530 ms       ->   71,758 ms, worst single block 7,080 -> 26,532 ms
   beats LATE once settled      9.9 %       ->     31.6 %, and 8.3% SWALLOWED WHOLE
   THE WALKED CITY ALONE     58.5 fps       ->    58.4 fps
 *** READ THE LAST ROW. THE WALKED CITY DOES NOT CARE ABOUT THE THROTTLE AT ALL. So what collapses on a phone is NOT the world and NOT the walking. It is THE FIGHT (an 8x fall) and THE SHELL BOOT. That is a much narrower target than "the game is slow", and it is only visible because the control is measured at both rates in one run.
 AND THE 120 BPM LAW ON A PHONE: one beat in twelve never happens. Nobody had that number because nobody kept a throttled pass.
 THE OLD RECORD WAS WRONG IN THE BUILD'S FAVOUR: it said the fight ran at 16.2 fps with 7,424 draw calls a frame. It is 57.2 fps at 4. SOMEBODY FIXED THE FIGHT AND NOBODY RE-MEASURED FOR NINE DAYS. A stale measurement is reassurance about a build that no longer exists, in both directions.
 A DEFECT IN THIS LANE'S OWN GATE, NAMED NOT HALF-FIXED: the fight budget the gate holds is 10 fps and the build does 57, so A 5.7x REGRESSION WOULD PASS GREEN. The budget is "worst case across the last six refreshes", whose own argument is explicitly about ONE UNCHANGED TREE, but a history entry carries no build identity, so a sample from the broken build anchors the budget across a real fix. A new rule needs its own measurement of the real spread; inventing a clamp factor at the end of a long round is how a gate gets a number nobody can defend. NEXT LINE OF THIS ROW (rule 6).
 ONE LINE FOR RUN, named not fixed: the speed gate has two reds and they are ONE BUG. #daycard is inset:0 and SITS OVER ALL EIGHT DIRECTION BUTTONS ON BOOT, so a driven thumb has nothing to press and the alpha never reaches its first step.  HE MEETS THE WORST PART OF THE GAME FIRST, AND THE BOX WAS HIDING IT. This container is not a handset; every fps number this fleet ever posted was taken on a machine several times faster than his phone. The walk now takes a CPU throttle, and a ladder was run in one window:
   1x   door 13.4 s   58.4 fps over the walk   53.3 fps in the first 15 s   worst stall 1.2 s
   4x   door 52.9 s   53.4 fps over the walk    9.8 fps in the first 15 s   worst stall 8.8 s
   6x   door 79.4 s   34.9 fps over the walk   11.0 fps in the first 15 s   worst stall 8.1 s
 At 4x, second by second: 4, 8, 6, 4, 6, 8, 7, 10, 7, 7, 9, 7, 5, 2 -- THEN 57, 56, 57. THIRTEEN SECONDS AT ABOUT TEN FRAMES A SECOND, THEN IT SNAPS TO FIFTY-SEVEN. The 6x run has the same shape. At 1x the dip is three seconds and small, which is why nobody has ever seen it. A whole-walk average buries it completely, and thirteen seconds is a sixth of his five minutes and the first thing he touches. THIS IS NOT MINE TO FIX: it lives in the demo shell's boot and the city frame's first paint. ONE LINE FOR RUN and ONE FOR LIFE+CITY.
 AND HIS THEORY, NAMED: the door opens after 3 files; then 30 more files and 75.9 MB stream in behind him while he plays, the last landing 227 s after the door (at 4x: 31 files, 80.9 MB, last at 311 s, past the end of his five minutes). NEW GATE, in the suite as LOADING IN PLAY: gates/loading_during_play_gate.js, a ratchet pinned off two of its own runs (63.9 MB, 27 files in a 75 s window), four floors before any ceiling, GREEN 6/0.
 WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK, SAID OUT LOUD: the test server sets no cache headers and this container's network policy blocks the live site, so whether a real browser re-downloads those chunks or reads them from disk is UNKNOWN from here. Either way the bytes are parsed on the main thread while he plays.
 AND A TEST I BUILT AND THREW AWAY BEFORE IT REACHED THIS PAGE: I tried to prove his theory by splitting the walk into loading seconds and quiet seconds. Two ways of lining up the load clock with the frame clock gave two answers off the SAME run (45.3 vs 55.3, gap 10.0; and 51.7 vs 55.4, gap 3.7). A test that changes its verdict with its arithmetic is not evidence, so it is deleted. The second-by-second curve above needs no alignment at all.

I'll put them on Sonnet... no blind spots'; laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_THE_FIGHT_GETS_DEEP_TUNING_AND_MODS_9_27_26.md; his words records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_450_HOURS_THE_FIGHT_GETS_DEEP_9_27_26.md). (a) DEPTH IS THE TARGET: formation and gear on the grid, knowledge that pays, RF4 speed with BB depth; COMBAT [formation] and [gambits] (FF12 gambits: the company acts on its own). (b) DEATH SOFTENED, default in VOTE: struck down = 20% dead, 80% a debilitating injury out 30 to 40 game days with a permanent mark. (c) ORIGINS at stated difficulties (PEOPLE the people, TUNING the numbers); DIFFICULTY SLIDERS are TUNING's to design; ARMOUR ATTACHMENTS are CHARACTER's (school then cook); weapons stay shapes and reach. READBACK: NOTHING IS HEARD UNTIL IT IS SAID BACK AND THE SENDER SAYS CORRECT (the coordinator's school, round two of ten, from air traffic control, the operating room and the Army back-brief; records/BOHEMIA_COORDINATOR_SCHOOL_SECOND_ROUND_READBACK_10_10_26.md: 71% of readbacks in one FAA study were faulty, Tenerife's 583 dead came from one ambiguous phrase, the surgical checklist's check-back cut deaths from 1.5% to 0.8%). Three legs, from this round. (a) THE LANE'S READBACK: a claim commit carries one line in the lane's own words, never a paste of the row, thirty words or fewer: 'READBACK [label]: I read this as: <what will be built and how it is measured>; done means <one testable thing>.' If the row does not fit in thirty words the row was too long: the lane writes 'SAY AGAIN [label]: <the clause it cannot read>' and does not start. (b) THE COORDINATOR'S HEARBACK: every sweep, before any other commit is read, every READBACK since the last sweep gets one of two words on the lane's row: CORRECT, or 'NEGATIVE: <the one thing wrong, in a new sentence>'. A NEGATIVE restarts the loop before code is touched. A claim with no readback is not a claim: 'NO READBACK, ROW OPEN'. The sweep's tally gains 'readbacks heard: N of N claims; negatives: N'. (c) THE READBACK TO PAOLO: every reply that turns his sentence into a rule or a job carries, right above WHAT I NEED FROM YOU, 'WHAT I HEARD: <his instruction in one plain sentence>', three at most; he corrects with one word or ignores it, and silence through his next VAMILY means CORRECT. The sounds misread (rule 88 amended) would have died at this line. Reserved words on this board: READBACK, SAY AGAIN, CORRECT, NEGATIVE, WHAT I HEARD mean only this. (HOLD keeps its rule-88 meaning; the school's suggestion to rename it is declined as churn.) Gate: PLUMBER [the readback leg]. FOLDED 10/10 by rule 97: the claim's readback line is now the one-breath line 'I read this as... I intend to... Two up: ...'; legs (b) and (c) stand.

THE STOP CORD: THE LINE STOPS WHERE THE DEFECT IS SEEN, NEVER WHERE IT IS REPORTED (the coordinator's school, round five of ten, from the Toyota floor: Georgetown pulls the cord about 2,000 times a week and Ford's Dearborn about twice, NUMMI's same workers went from the worst plant to 117 problems per 100 cars against the industry's 151; records/BOHEMIA_COORDINATOR_SCHOOL_FIFTH_ROUND_THE_STOP_CORD_10_10_26.md). Any lane, EYES, PLUMBER or the coordinator who SEES a defect on the real surface (the throttled phone loading the live link; a thing seen, never a suspicion from code) pulls the cord: one block at the TOP of 00_START_HERE_NEXT_SESSION.md, 'STOP (lane, time): I SAW <the defect, one sentence, with the number> ON <the profile and the link> AT <the second>. The line is stopped for <the files the defect lives in>.' No fix and no theory in the block. Pulling is an obligation: the lane that saw it and pushed anyway is the violation, never the lane that pulled wrongly. WHAT STOPS: pushes to the named files and the demo cut (no G-O, rule 93); everything else moves (the school's 'all of slices/ and engine/' is cut to the defect's files, because a fleet of 26 cannot stop for one pipe). AT THE STATION, within the round: the coordinator loads the live link on the throttled phone and reproduces the defect before reading any lane's explanation; NOT SEEN restarts the line; seen, the five whys go under the block as far as honestly reached, guesses marked. RESTART when the cause is written (a symptom is a fuse), the fix was seen on the phone with the number, and one gate goes red if it returns; the block then moves to a records file. THE CHALK CIRCLE: every sweep opens with the coordinator's own five minutes on the throttled phone with the file list open, fixing nothing (rule 90 round 1, now with the network panel); a number that disagrees with a lane's is a pull. THE POKA-YOKE, ONE STOPWATCH: load time, files after the door, bytes and requests per tile are read by ONE script on the throttled profile into ONE line in ONE file; a lane quotes that line and never a number of its own; a gate refuses a commit carrying another load number (PLUMBER [the one stopwatch]). The first pull is on the handoff now: the double tile download and the three mid-play reloads.

THE TURNAROUND TABLE: THE TURN IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE CLIMB, AND THE FIRST TANK TO HIT THIRDS TURNS EVERYONE (the coordinator's school, round six of ten, from Everest's 2 p.m. rule and its eight dead, the cockpit's go-around that 95 to 97 percent of crews skip, the cave diver's rule of thirds, the firefighter's air alarm, the trial's stopping rule set before the data; records/BOHEMIA_COORDINATOR_SCHOOL_SIXTH_ROUND_THE_TURNAROUND_TIME_10_10_26.md). THE TABLE: (1) A CLAIM: three sweeps from claim to shipped-or-back; the row says 'CLAIMED <date>, TURNS <the third sweep>'; the words: 'TURN. Ship what is in the tab or hand the row back', and the row returns OPEN with a two-line post-mortem. Applied now: every CLAIMED row dated before 10/4 is TURNED on this board. (2) AN ATTEMPT: two versions; the fourth (STOP PRODUCING) is the alarm, the second is the half tank; the VOTE item says 'V2 IS THE LAST' at version one; the words: 'TWO WAS THE LAST. Graveyard it or ask him one question'; no third is drawn; a feature he named by name gets both versions and one bold question (the summit is optional, the handoff is mandatory). (3) A HOLD: one round, then it lifts by itself unless the coordinator re-writes it with its reason at the sweep; a hold with no expiry line is void on sight; rule 88's holds are re-affirmed in every sweep record with his words or they lift (the sounds hold, which should have lifted, is the case). (4) A SWEEP: ten files or twenty minutes of reading, whichever first, then write; five notes at most (rule 92's eight folds to five here); the words: 'TEN. WRITE.' (5) A RESEARCH ROUND: one agent, one file, 8 to 12 cited findings; a burst of N agents is ONE round (his words, 10/10). (6) HIS ATTENTION: one bold question a reply, three things to look at, each in a named tab; past three the coordinator decides and builds, correct-after. Gate: PLUMBER [the turn leg].

THE TRAIL EVAPORATES: EVERY MARK HAS A HALF-LIFE, AND ONLY A LANE'S COMMIT RENEWS IT (the coordinator's school, round seven of ten, from the ant trail that forgets an empty food source, the ant mill that follows itself in a circle until it dies, Dorigo's evaporation rate without which the colony stagnates, and the bees' dance that decays so no scout can lobby forever; records/BOHEMIA_COORDINATOR_SCHOOL_SEVENTH_ROUND_THE_TRAIL_EVAPORATES_10_10_26.md; measured this hour: 1,665 board lines, 95 rules, a 135,343-line handoff with 5,070 July-and-August lines against 445 October ones, 433 law files with 16 archive lines ever). A CITE is mechanical: a commit on main by a lane other than the coordinator naming the mark (a rule number, a [two-word] label, a file path); the coordinator's own citations do not count. THE RATES: a RULE uncited for 7 sweeps folds to one line (title plus the pointer to its file), 14 and it leaves the page (a rule quoting Paolo keeps its law file and gets its archive-registry line; a coordinator rule with no Paolo quote lives only in its record); a ROW open and unclaimed for 10 sweeps is marked STALE, 14 and it moves to records/BOHEMIA_EVAPORATED_ROWS.md as one line (a CLAIMED row keeps rule 95's turn); the SUITE, CUT, BREAK and COOK LINES hold the newest sweep only, the older entry moves to that sweep's record the moment a new one lands; a RECORD or LAW uncited by any live file or lane commit for 30 days leaves the canon index for archive/ with its registry line; a HANDOFF BLOCK: the START file keeps each lane's two newest blocks, older ones go to handoffs/<LANE>_ARCHIVE.md (the 9/13 split, built now, with the handoff gate changed in the same commit so the move is not a deletion). THE QUORUM: a coordinator rule becomes a law file only after three distinct lanes cite it in commits; Paolo's words skip the quorum. THE STOP SIGNAL: a lane that measures a mark dead writes 'STOP <mark> <sha> <why>' in its commit; the sweep stamps the mark DEAD with a pointer; a second STOP from another lane removes it from the page. THE MACHINE: records/target/BOHEMIA_TRAIL.json, one row per mark with last_cite, lanes_citing and strength, written by tools/bohemia_trail_sweep.js at every VAMILY and never by hand (PLUMBER [the trail file]). DONE BY HAND TODAY, the first evaporation: THE SUITE LINE and THE CUT LINE keep the newest sweep, THE BREAK LIST keeps his October plays, rules 53, 58 and 60 fold to one line; the removed text is verbatim in records/BOHEMIA_EVAPORATED_10_10_26.md. THE ANT MILL WE ARE IN, named: the sweep lines, each shaped like the last, reinforced every round while the food at the trail's end, his thumb, is exhausted (173 waiting); rule 92's sort and this rule's evaporation are the way out. AMENDED 10/10 sweep AH (WORLD ad687f3e found the conflict and was right): a ROW in a lane whose MODE is HOLD does not evaporate, the hold pauses its clock, because rule 88 forbids the lane the only act that would save it; and a lane's commit naming a row's label is a CITE that renews the row, not only a rule. The row clause reads: open, unclaimed AND uncited for 10 sweeps in a running lane.
97. THE ROW IS INTENT: THE ROW SAYS WHY AND WHAT HE SEES; THE LANE SAYS HOW, OUT LOUD, THEN GOES (the coordinator's school, round eight of ten, from the USS Santa Fe's 'I intend to' that made ten of its officers captains, Prussian mission command, Nelson's memorandum before Trafalgar and the Ritz's two thousand dollars a bellman may spend without asking; records/BOHEMIA_COORDINATOR_SCHOOL_EIGHTH_ROUND_I_INTEND_TO_10_10_26.md). From this round a row the coordinator writes is three parts and no more: PURPOSE (the why, tied to Paolo's words), END STATE (what he sees or hears on his phone, in which tab, when it is done), CONSTRAINT (the one law or limit that must not break). The HOW belongs to the lane. The coordinator MAY write purpose, end state, constraint and a pointer to the record with his words; it MAY NOT write a tool, a file, a patch, a measuring method, a number the lane can measure itself, or a sequence of steps; 'use', 'via', 'with the' and 'then' in a row are the tell. THE TEST: cover the how with your thumb; if what is left still says when it is done and what Paolo sees, it was intent; if nothing is left to aim at, it was an order in a row's clothes. THE CLAIM merges rule 91's readback into one breath, in this order: 'I read this as <the end state in the lane's words>. I intend to <the how, one sentence>. Two up: Paolo wants <his words>; the coordinator wants <the purpose>.' A lane that cannot name both intents has a task, not intent, and says so instead of building. A measured finding that the row was wrong is the lane's to act on, never to wait on: one handoff line, 'I intended X, measured Y, now doing Z', and it keeps going (rule 12 made law). DELIBERATE ACTION for a push to main: the commit message carries the row's end state and the one thing that would prove it is not met. THE PASS IS THE COORDINATOR, which cooks nothing; DIRECTION tastes every part at the line check against its twin; RUN is the runner and carries into the demo only a plate the pass has called HANDS (rule 93: a plate is a cue). THE LINE CHECK before any round he may open the game: every fired plate's parts tasted on one phone from a written sheet (its tab, 60 on a phone, analog horror, the law it must not break); what fails is 86'd and told to him in one plain sentence, never found by him. IN THE WEEDS: a station writes it the round it knows; the pass answers within the round with help or a kill; a third round in the weeds is a kill. The words and nothing else: FIRE, HOLD, N-OUT, HEARD, IN THE WEEDS, REFIRE, 86, DEAD, HANDS, ALL DAY. THE PIXEL FLOOR IS THE PACKS: NOTHING WE MAKE IS TINIER THAN WHAT WE DOWNLOADED (PAOLO 10/10, LOCKED: 'every time you make something art-wise you use the tiniest amount of pixels possible and it's really upsetting; look at the graphics we downloaded and see how many pixels they are; that is the floor, the minimum'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_PIXEL_FLOOR_IS_THE_PACKS_10_10_26.md, which holds the measurement). MEASURED THIS HOUR over the 1,922 tiles in reference/art_bank: the pack is a 96-pixel world. Road tiles median 95 by 96 (smallest 66 by 69); ground 95 by 88 (smallest 40 by 38); markings 96 by 83; settlement pieces 92 by 92; doors 96 by 89; lamps 59 by 96; props 94 by 91 (smallest 29 by 36). THE FLOOR, BY KIND, a minimum never a target: a floor tile 96 by 96; a building piece, door or wall 96 on its long side; a lamp 96 tall; a prop never under 29 by 36 and a car or crate about 96 wide; an ICON never under 32 by 32 (today 5 by 5); a MAP MARKER never under 40 by 40 (today 8 by 8); a portrait never under 96 by 96 at its own pixels; a person stays the 112 box. The camera may shrink the world on the map (THE GROUND MAY ZOOM); the asset in the file is never under its floor. NO ATARI (the third votes) gets its number here. The floor goes on DIRECTION's card and on every study page (rule 100c); PLUMBER [the pixel floor] refuses a new asset under its kind's floor; every placeholder under the floor is listed as such in records/BOHEMIA_PLACEHOLDERS.md (the icons and the markers first).

EVERYTHING THAT FACES IS MADE IN ALL EIGHT DIRECTIONS (PAOLO 10/10, LOCKED: 'one of the chats made a dire wolf; when you create something it has to be made in all eight directions, you understand that'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_WHY_SO_TINY_AND_EIGHT_DIRECTIONS_10_10_26.md). A person, a beast, a vehicle, anything that turns: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW, drawn, each with its idle, step and the clip it owns; a mirrored half is not a direction, and a sheet that lacks one facing is not a candidate (rule 100) and does not register (rule 89). The square grid (rule 37) is the reason: a thing walks eight ways, so it is drawn eight ways. PLUMBER [the eight facings] counts them on every sheet that moves.
108. THE TOOLCHAIN: THE CHATS DRIVE REAL ART AND SOUND TOOLS AGAINST HIS PACKS, AND NOBODY DRAWS A TILE PIXEL BY PIXEL IN CODE AGAIN (PAOLO 10/10: 'find out what tools high-quality people that vibe code use, what do I have to buy, what needs to get installed in my repo that makes great art and great sounds; all these months it's been failing me; I'm gonna need outside help implemented into our system'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_FIND_THE_TOOLS_GREAT_VIBE_CODERS_USE_FOR_ART_AND_SOUND_10_10_26.md; the research: records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_THE_TOOLS_THAT_MAKE_GREAT_ART_AND_SOUND_10_10_26.md, three shopping tiers, prices with URLs, the wiring table). THE FINDING: the good small teams buy packs (he did, 87), feed the packs as reference images into a pixel-art model trained only on pixel art (Retro Diffusion takes nine reference tiles and a locked palette; PixelLab makes 8-direction characters and Wang tilesets; both have MCP servers a chat drives alone), clean in Aseprite (headless, scriptable), and for sound start from real recordings (Sonniss GDC bundles and Freesound CC0, free) or a text-to-sound model, then run the file through a tape and a real-room reverb (Pedalboard, Chow Tape Model, offline, in batch). We treated art as a programming problem; that is the whole mistake. THE LAW: (a) a cook's tile, prop, house, portrait or icon is GENERATED against his pack tiles as the style reference with the pack's palette locked, then cleaned, then put beside the pack twin on its one-at-a-time sheet (rules 100, 101, 105); a tile drawn rectangle by rectangle in a Python or JavaScript tool is no longer a candidate; (b) a sound starts from a recording or a model's render and goes through the analog horror chain; the 83 oscillator and noise calls in the sound engine are the retire list, one per sound as its recording lands; (c) the free tier installs this round (PLUMBER [the toolchain]): Retro Diffusion's and PixelLab's free credits by MCP, pixelize for the palette snap, the Sonniss bundles and Freesound into a library folder with their licences, Pedalboard with Chow Tape; keys in .env, one install line each, a README; (d) LICENCES: Eleven Music and Meta's MusicGen and AudioGen are not licensed for a sold game and do not ship; the nerijs SDXL pixel LoRA's licence is disputed and does not ship; every library file carries its licence line; (e) WHAT HE BUYS is his call and is listed to him once (the under-100 tier: Aseprite $19.99 once, Retro Diffusion credits about $30 a month, PixelLab about $12 a month, ElevenLabs $6 or $22 a month); nothing paid is assumed until he says yes. ROUND TWO (10/10, 'do one more round of research, please'; records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_THE_EXACT_PIPELINE_ROUND_TWO_10_10_26.md): the exact calls and commands, and two corrections to round one: Retro Diffusion's real style ids are lowercase (rd_tile__tile_variation, rd_pro__topdown, rd_pro__horror; the names RD_FLUX and RD_FAST in round one were wrong) with input_palette, tile_x and tile_y, input_image, up to nine reference_images and a free check_cost dry run; and OpenAIR is dead (EchoThief is alive and allows derivative work). PixelLab turns one front-facing drawing into eight directions and animates from a skeleton, tops out at 128 to 256 px, and its own docs expect hand fixes. STORES: Steam and itch.io require an AI disclosure tag when generated art or audio ships; the game carries it honestly. THE DAY ONE PLAN is section E of the record: one road tile from nine of his (the call, the palette lock, the seam test, the 1:1 sheet with pass and fail written in advance) and one door sound (a Sonniss recording through tape, an EchoThief room, a high-pass, a limiter, A/B against our synthesised door). The three rows run it: PLUMBER [the toolchain], COOK [generate against the pack], SOUNDS [from a recording]. ONE-TIME OR FREE (Paolo 10/10: 'something that gets implemented into my repo, a one-time purchase, not a monthly thing, nothing that uses outside credits'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_ONE_TIME_PURCHASE_NO_MONTHLY_NO_OUTSIDE_CREDITS_10_10_26.md): the shopping rule is BUY ONCE OR FREE, IN THE REPO, ON OUR OWN COMPUTE. Kept: Aseprite ($19.99 once, headless, the chats write its Lua), Retro Diffusion's Aseprite extension ($65 once, the model running locally and unlimited; it needs a graphics card, which the chats' cloud machines do not have, so it runs on his computer from scripts the chats write), and the free set downloaded once into the repo's library folder (Sonniss, Freesound CC0, EchoThief, Pedalboard with Chow Tape, pixelize, bfxr, ImageMagick). Dropped: every subscription and every per-call credit (Retro Diffusion online, PixelLab, ElevenLabs, Scenario, Mubert, Soundly); the free trial credits are used once for the day-one test and never again. The honest line stands in the record: pack-quality pixel art comes from a model on a graphics card or from an artist, never from code alone; if his computer has no graphics card, the one-time route for new art is a one-time artist commission for the hero set and the chats assemble. THE TUTOR (round three, Paolo 10/10: 'a simple coding source, a teacher or tutor for you; I don't want a graphics card'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_A_TUTOR_FOR_THE_CHATS_NO_GRAPHICS_CARD_10_10_26.md; the research: records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_THE_TUTOR_NO_GPU_NO_SUBSCRIPTION_ROUND_THREE_10_10_26.md). The local-model route is out with the graphics card. THE TUTOR IS THREE THINGS BOLTED TOGETHER, no GPU, no service: (1) A RULEBOOK THE CHATS LOAD AS A SKILL, skills/pixel-tutor/: the measured rules of his 87 packs (the palette ramps as files, the outline weight, light from the top-left, the 45-degree floor-to-wall ratio, the 96 floor), the Pixel Logic techniques as checklists (cluster size, when to anti-alias, banding, pillow shading, dither only on large flat areas, selective outlines, sub-pixel steps), the Saint11 tutorials with their CC-BY credit, the before-and-after sheet template, and the sound half (layering from recordings, the tape chain, the sfxr grammar for UI clicks). (2) CPU TOOLS THAT DRAW AND MEASURE: Aseprite headless in the containers (one $19.99 licence, built from source as its EULA allows, the binary never published), the open aseprite-mcp (assess_sprite, diff_sprites, validate_loop), Pyxelate for the palette snap, texture synthesis and Wave Function Collapse for ground variants from pack samples, an autotile tool for the 47-piece sets, a seam test, Tiled's rasterizer for map proofs, Pedalboard and SoX for sound. (3) A GATE, pixel_tutor_gate, that rejects the tells before he sees them: a colour outside the declared ramp, orphan pixels, jaggies on 45-degree lines, pillow shading, mixed outline weights, a loop whose last frame repeats the first, a sound with no recorded layer. And ONE ARTIST PAID ONCE for the hero set (one character in eight directions with walk and attack, one ground and wall tileset, one prop set, one portrait), delivered as Aseprite files with palette and tags, which the chats extend by recolour, autotile, mirror, frame-diff and seam test, never freehand. ONE-TIME PRICE: Pixel Logic about $10, Aseprite $19.99, the rest free; the artist $800 to $2,500. THE HONEST LIMIT: knowledge plus tools raise the floor and kill the seventh-grader tells; the ceiling is the artist; CPU image models are unproven for 96-pixel tiles and teach no taste; a rulebook nobody enforces is a comment, so the gate is what makes it real. Rows: DIRECTION [the pixel tutor], PLUMBER [the toolchain] re-aimed, COOK [the hero brief]. THE SIX OPTIONS (Paolo 10/11: 'give me six options for the graphics asset tile maker, the best art tool, immediately'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_SIX_OPTIONS_FOR_THE_ART_TOOL_10_11_26.md): Aseprite $19.99 once; Tilesetter $12.99 once (seamless autotile sets from a few of his tiles, no graphics card); Retro Diffusion's Aseprite extension $65 once (needs a graphics card); Retro Diffusion's online API (prepaid per image, outside credits); PixelLab (a subscription, eight-direction people); a pixel artist once ($800 to $2,500). The coordinator's pick: 1 and 2 today, 6 for the hero set, 3 to 5 only if he bends a rule. Tilesetter joins the toolchain row. NOT JUST TILES (Paolo 10/11: 'I want everything: the guns, the portraits, people's faces, the characters, different angles of the buildings, wrecked vehicles, street lights'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_NOT_JUST_TILES_EVERYTHING_10_11_26.md): the tool covers EVERY asset kind or it is a helper, not the tool; Tilesetter is a helper for tiles only and the coordinator's pick of it was too narrow. The tools that make every kind from his packs as the reference are Retro Diffusion (tiles, props, vehicles, weapons, buildings, lamps, portraits) and PixelLab (eight-direction people and beasts). Under his three rules none works, so the coordinator's pick asks for the smallest bend: a ONE-TIME PREPAID BALANCE on Retro Diffusion online (no monthly, bought once, cents an asset, the chats drive it alone), plus Aseprite once to clean; the eight-direction people from PixelLab only if he allows the one subscription, else from the artist once. COOK [generate against the pack] widens to one asset of each kind in turn: a street lamp, a wrecked car, a gun, a portrait, a house face, a tile. HIS YES (10/11: 'I'm definitely down for this... if it's a tool I can connect that would be awesome; if it's more work for me I cannot do it'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_YES_TO_RETRO_DIFFUSION_IF_IT_IS_NOT_WORK_FOR_ME_10_11_26.md): the one prepaid balance on Retro Diffusion is approved. His part once: the account, the balance, the key pasted into the repo's GitHub secret RD_TOKEN. Ours: a GitHub Action (the chats' machines cannot reach outside hosts, GitHub's runners can) that takes a chat's request file, calls the API with the pack references and the locked palette, snaps, seam-tests and commits the 1:1 sheet to the cook folder; check_cost before every call; a spend cap at his balance; the key never leaves the secret store. He never touches the tool again. NOTHING CHARGED BEFORE HIS YES (10/11: 'it costs money for you to present it to me; this cannot be the workflow'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_NOTHING_IS_CHARGED_BEFORE_I_APPROVE_IT_10_11_26.md): a chat may not generate and then show him. The order is REQUEST CARD (free: what will be made, the nine pack references shown, the palette, the size, the exact cost from the free cost check), HIS YES on that card, THEN the one call, THEN the result card for his YES, NO or FINAL. The Action reads only approved request cards from the registry and spends only what each card said; a NO at either step costs nothing further. The free credits of a new account are used first, so the first sheets cost zero while he judges the tool. The chats' request cards are their one-at-a-time asks (rule 101) in the VOTE tab, tagged red one per lane (rule 92). NO FREE-UNTIL-DOWNLOAD (checked 10/11 against the site and the API docs): Retro Diffusion charges every generation from a prepaid balance (from $0.03), shows the exact price before the call, refunds failures, gives 50 free credits at signup with no card, never expires credits; no free preview or watermark model. The 50 free credits are the only see-before-you-pay; the first sheets use them and he decides after. A FAILED GENERATION IS HIS CALL (10/11: 'if it makes something and I say that's a failure, that would be awesome; I can afford lots of these generations, that's not the issue'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_A_FAILED_GENERATION_IS_MY_CALL_10_11_26.md): his NO on a result card is a failed generation: to the graveyard with his note, never shown again as it was; the chat may re-request once with his note on the new card (rule 95: two is the last), then a different reference set or the artist. The site refunds only technical failures; the cents are not the point by his word. THE TEN STEPS (10/11, his 'how can you incorporate this into the workflow'): records/BOHEMIA_THE_ART_WORKFLOW_IN_TEN_STEPS_10_11_26.md is the one page every art chat follows: the list, the study, the free request card, his YES, the one call, the clean and the tells gate, the result card, his word (YES not final, NO failed, FINAL), into the game only on FINAL, the sweep's report. WHY IT WON (10/11, his 'did you just suck at online research'): the honest readback, the whole field in one table and the one miss (PixelLab's per-call API, billing unconfirmed), is records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_WHY_RETRO_DIFFUSION_AND_WHAT_I_MISSED_10_11_26.md; card one of the six is the eight-facing test. ROUND FOUR: THE GUN IN THE REPO (10/11, Paolo: 'why can't I just get you a tutor or get something in our project files, like a gun, I'll buy you a gun, why does it have to keep being this outside option'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_WHY_NOT_A_GUN_IN_THE_REPO_10_11_26.md). THE ANSWER: a tutor gives the chats rules, not eyes and a hand; the hand is a trained model, and the model CAN be ours: open pixel-art models under free licences plus a LoRA taught once on his packs, run on GitHub's FREE standard runners on CPU (this repo is public), minutes a picture, zero dollars, no card on his computer, driven by the same free request card and his YES. THE LAW: the repo gets its own picture engine (PLUMBER [the gun in the repo]); Retro Diffusion is the SECOND engine, prepaid, fired only where the gun fails the pack twin after two tries; the card names the engine and the price (zero for the gun); the ten steps do not change. The one-time buys stand as his optional shopping list (Aseprite, Pixel Logic, one GPU hour to teach the LoRA, an artist for the heroes). ROUND FIVE: THE ONE-TIME LIST (10/11, Paolo: 'is there not a single thing in the universe I can make a one time purchase for to make you better as a graphic artist'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_ONE_THING_IN_THE_UNIVERSE_TO_BUY_ONCE_10_11_26.md): nothing bought once changes a chat's own hand; what works is a HAND or a TEACHER, and six exist: (1) the LoRA taught on his packs, $2 to $5 once or free on Kaggle, the biggest; (2) Aseprite $19.99; (3) more packs $10 to $60 each, aimed at the holes (wrecks, guns, portraits, eight facings); (4) Pixel Logic $10, its rules go into the tutor skill and the clean gate; (5) a graphics card box $300 to $600 as the repo's own runner, HIS call alone; (6) an artist's seed style sheet $300 to $800, the twin and the training food. These six are THE list; nobody puts another purchase to him; he answers with numbers; the free road runs regardless. ROUND SIX: ASEPRITE (10/11, Paolo's one word 'Aseprite' to the one-time list; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_ASEPRITE_10_11_26.md): number 2 is bought, $19.99 once; the other five are not picked and are never asked again (he says a number if he wants one). PLUMBER [aseprite in the pipe]: built from source on the free runner (the EULA allows it for own use) and cached, Lua scripts in tools/aseprite/ for palette snap, outline, stray pixels, blur-free resize, eight-facing sheets, frame export and the clean report; step 6 of the ten steps runs through them; proven by one pack tile round-tripped with a byte-identical palette and one generated picture cleaned end to end with no human. He installs it on his computer and pastes nothing. ROUND SEVEN: PIXEL LOGIC (10/11, Paolo's second pick, 'Pixel Logic, give me the links to these'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_PIXEL_LOGIC_AND_THE_LINKS_10_11_26.md): two bought, Aseprite $19.99 (aseprite.org) and Pixel Logic $10 (michafrar.gumroad.com/l/pixel-logic); the other four numbers are closed unless he names one. The PDF is NEVER committed (public repo); he drags it into the DIRECTION chat once, and DIRECTION [the pixel tutor] writes the book's RULES in our own words with page cites into the tutor skill and the clean gate's named faults (banding, pillow shading, jaggies, ramps and hue shift, anti-aliasing, silhouettes, dither limits, sub-pixel motion); until it lands, DIRECTION works from the public preview and marks the skill DRAFT. PIXEL LOGIC IS THE SOURCE (10/11, rule 108 ROUND SEVEN): he bought the book; when the PDF lands in your chat, read it and write its rules in our own words with page cites into the skill and the clean gate's fault list; never commit the PDF or quote its text or pictures; until it lands, the public preview and the table of contents, skill marked DRAFT. HIS CHALLENGE ON THE TWO BUYS (10/11, 'is there some ancient forbidden knowledge sauce in the book' and 'what the fuck is Aseprite, is that a game'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_IS_THERE_SECRET_SAUCE_IN_THE_BOOK_AND_WHAT_IS_ASEPRITE_10_11_26.md): no secret in the book, its rules are the standard ones the chats already know, it buys one page-numbered source; the failure was the hand, not the rules; Aseprite is the standard pixel editor, not a game, step 6 of the ten steps runs through its scripts headless. BOTH BUYS ARE OPTIONAL TO THE PIPE: the runner's Aseprite is built free from the public source either way, and DIRECTION writes the tutor skill from the known rules now; the book, if it lands, adds page cites and test pictures. Nobody asks him to buy either. ROUND NINE: THE WORKFLOW IS THE GAME, ZERO NEW STEPS FOR HIM (10/11, Paolo: 'I don't need the best, I need you to be the best artist you possibly can be... the workflow is how this game is even going to get shipped at all and if we have to add one or two more steps every time we need a graphics asset made I'm gonna shoot myself in the face'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_WORKFLOW_IS_HOW_THE_GAME_SHIPS_ZERO_NEW_STEPS_10_11_26.md). THE LAW: his work per asset is ONE TAP in the VOTE tab (yes / no / final on the result card) and can only go down from here; the request-card YES (step 4) exists ONLY when a card costs money, the free engine fires without it; every tool the research proposes is filtered FIRST by his step count, zero or out; a step for the chats is fine, a step for him is not; one-time support (a purchase, a computer left on) is welcome, dependence on it is not. The goal is the chats' CEILING, not perfect art. SAID AGAIN, HARDER (10/11, 'any tools, any standardized thing for all the art chats, any awesome sauce, I'll do anything... but if every art asset is a song and dance with 234 extra steps the game will never be published'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_ANY_TOOL_ANY_SAUCE_BUT_NOT_234_STEPS_10_11_26.md): the offer is any one-time tool or standard thing the chats carry (one skill file, one pack-rule sheet, one twin gate, one eight-facing rig); the line is zero steps for him per asset, the ship condition; the gather sorts every finding by HIS STEPS ADDED first, nonzero is cut. ROUND EIGHT: UNLOCK THE LIMITS (10/11, Paolo: 'the limit of your graphics feels coded by a seventh grader, I'm trying to unlock your limits'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_UNLOCK_YOUR_LIMITS_10_11_26.md; eight research pages records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_UNLOCK_THE_LIMITS_01..08_*_10_11_26.md, gathered in records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_UNLOCK_THE_LIMITS_00_THE_GATHER_10_11_26.md). THE FINDING: the chats were failing at the one thing a language model is worst at, placing pixels as numbers in code; every road that works moves the pixels to a machine built for it. THE LAW: (a) NO CHAT DRAWS A PIXEL OR A CURVE IN CODE; pixels come from Aseprite's scripts, a vector-parts shrink, a 3D render, a pack cut or the gun; a pixel written as a number in JavaScript is a gate failure (PLUMBER [the art pipe gate]); (b) ONE CAMERA, REAL METERS, THE MODEL TURNS: DIRECTION owns a master Blender rig (orthographic X 60 / Z 45, one sun, meters locked to the 96-pixel floor), eight facings come from the model turning, headless on the free runner; (c) THE PACKS ARE THE RULER: PLUMBER [the twin gate] scores every piece against its pack twin and family with thresholds measured from the packs against themselves, RED never reaches his tab; (d) THE HAND: an Aseprite tool server plus ONE skill file every art chat loads plus ONE pack-rule sheet of measured numbers (DIRECTION [the pixel tutor]); (e) STRETCH THE PACKS first: kitbash, decals, 47-tile autotiles, faction recolour as a shade remap (the packs hold 2,455 to 3,073 colours a tile, quantise first); (f) the gun is a style LoRA on FLUX.2 klein base 4B (Apache-2.0) taught once on the packs, with an SD 1.5 twin for the CPU runner; eight facings are NOT solved by any public model, so (b) carries them; (g) his always-on box, if ever, registers to a PRIVATE twin repo, ephemeral, with an online check that falls back to the free runner; its label never appears in the public repo and it is never the only runner; (h) every row was admitted because it adds ZERO steps for him (ROUND NINE). ROUND EIGHT (10/11): the recipe is a style LoRA on FLUX.2 klein base 4B (Apache-2.0; undistilled base build; ai-toolkit or OneTrainer; 15 to 40 pack tiles nearest-neighbour upscaled 8x; one trigger word; about 1800 steps, under an hour on a rented 4090 or a free Kaggle T4 on the low-VRAM path) with an SD 1.5 TWIN LoRA on the same dataset for the CPU runner (FastSD CPU with OpenVINO; SD-Turbo and LCM for speed); build the SD 1.5 twin first, write the klein recipe and wait for his ONCE; eight facings are not solved by any public model, the rig carries them; records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_UNLOCK_THE_LIMITS_04_TEACHING_A_MODEL_HIS_PACKS_10_11_26.md. ROUND EIGHT (10/11): the deliverable is ONE skill file skills/bohemia-pixel-art/SKILL.md every art chat loads, holding the numbers table (112 px person, about 100 painted, 96 px floor, top-left light, the 45-degree ratio, square grid, one-pixel border, integer scaling, twelve keys a bar), the pack palettes as .gpl, the build order, a fault catalogue wired to bohemia_pixel_craft_audit.py and bohemia_eyes_pixel_tells.py, the render-critique-fix loop, the asset contract and a what-not-to-do list; rules from the pixel craft laws, Pixel Logic read once in a chat and restated with page cites, Saint11 (CC BY 4.0) and free rules pages; plus the PACK-RULE SHEET of measured numbers shared with COOK TWO; records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_UNLOCK_THE_LIMITS_06_WHAT_GOES_IN_THE_REPO_SKILLS_AND_TOOL_SERVERS_10_11_26.md. ROUND EIGHT (10/11): the tool server goes in beside the scripts (PLUMBER [the art pipe gate] names it); every art chat reaches Aseprite through it. THE SHOPPING LIST (10/11, his 'what shit do I need to download or buy online to support you'): records/BOHEMIA_THE_SHOPPING_LIST_10_11_26.md is the whole of it: buy once Aseprite, Pixel Logic, packs for the four holes (COOK posts the links as ONE card), optionally the box; sign up once Retro Diffusion (RD_TOKEN) and optionally Kaggle or RunPod for the model lesson; download nothing, the repo installs its own tools on the free runners. ROUND TEN: A CHAT'S OPINION OF ITS OWN PICTURE IS NOT IN THE LOOP (10/11, Paolo: 'the program makes you more professional, not better; you still might make shit that looks like shit because you think it looks good'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_PROGRAM_DOES_NOT_GIVE_YOU_TASTE_10_11_26.md). THE LAW: taste comes from places a chat cannot fake and never from the maker: (1) the packs decide through the twin gate, the chat never says 'looks good'; (2) the chat does not draw, the picture comes from the rig, the parts shrink, the pack cut or the gun; (3) when two candidates exist a SEPARATE chat (EYES) judges PAIRWISE against the twin with one question, never a 1-to-10, never the maker, cap three, keep best; (4) every NO from him lands in the graveyard with ONE fault tag and that fault becomes a measured check the same round, so he teaches the machine once per fault, not once per picture; (5) the squint: every asset must read at 8x8 and 16x16; (6) one thing at a time to FINAL, and the FINAL pile is a second ruler; (7) a human seed sheet is the one-time taste buy if he ever wants it. A chat cannot acquire taste; it can stop being the judge and the hand. ROUND ELEVEN: USE THE PACKS, DO NOT IMITATE THEM (10/11, Paolo: 'we did this already, we tried to match and compare the assets I bought and make it similar, and it turns out dog shit, you actually forgot about the assets we purchased'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_WE_TRIED_MATCHING_THE_PACKS_AND_IT_MADE_THE_MESS_10_11_26.md). HE IS RIGHT: the 9/4 compare law, the twin (82) and the reference check were 'make it similar then compare', the chat still drew by code, the compare read filenames not pixels, and the bank was never in a tool's path. WITHDRAWN as a method: 'similar to', 'inspired by', 'matched to the twin'. THE LAW: (a) the pack pieces ARE the art; a chat's art job is placing, cutting, layering and shade-remapping bought pieces, never making pieces that look like them; (b) a new piece exists only when no pack has it, and then it is BOUGHT (COOK [the pack card]) or, when nothing sells, comes from the camera route or a human, to his tap; (c) EVERY asset carries the bank path it was cut from, the model it was rendered from, or the pack card that bought it; no path, no asset (PLUMBER [the twin gate] becomes a provenance and drift check, not a similarity judge); (d) the bank list, by family with pictures, is the FIRST section of the art skill file, so the packs cannot be forgotten; (e) every 'matched' piece made so far is a placeholder (10/10), twin to nothing. ROUND EIGHT (c) and ROUND TEN (1) are read through this: the packs are not a ruler to copy against, they are the material. ROUND ELEVEN (10/11): DEMOTED from similarity judge to PROVENANCE and DRIFT: every asset must carry the bank path, model file or pack card it came from (no path, no asset); the rulers check that a cut or recolour did not drift from its source family and that a camera-route piece sits at the pack's scale and light; nothing is ever scored for 'how similar to the pack' because nothing is made to be similar. ROUND TWELVE: THE CHAT LEARNS TO SEE WHILE IT DRAWS (10/11, Paolo: 'sometimes I don't even like the packs... you're telling me to keep buying shit and I can't... why can't you just be a better pixel artist? what can I do to help you?'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_WHY_CANT_YOU_JUST_BE_A_BETTER_PIXEL_ARTIST_10_11_26.md). AMENDS ROUND ELEVEN: the packs are MATERIAL, not the look of three arcs; where he dislikes a pack piece it is a placeholder; buying is one road taken rarely, never the answer. THE LAW: a chat gets better the way a person does: (1) EYES OPEN WHILE DRAWING, every asset built in a render-look-fix loop of twenty to forty cycles (1x, 8x, shrunk to 16x16, faults written in words each cycle), the loop log rides with the asset, a once-rendered sheet is a failed sheet; (2) STAGES: silhouette, big shapes and light, ramps, detail, outline, each looked at before the next; (3) STUDY NOT COPY: take real pixel art apart for craft and write each lesson into the skill file with a before/after the chat made, the skill file only grows; (4) form from the rig and the parts, clean pixels from Aseprite, judgement exercised in the loop; (5) HIS HELP ONCE, his eye: a MOODBOARD of ten to twenty pictures he loves for the three arcs (photos, film, paintings, not packs), dropped in this chat once, and a TASTE SESSION in the VOTE tab, twenty pairs, once; both become rules in the skill file. DIRECTION [see while you draw] [the moodboard and the taste session]. THE INTAKE (10/11, Paolo: 'I might give you 20,000 pictures'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_I_MIGHT_GIVE_YOU_20000_PICTURES_10_11_26.md): no limit; ONE Google Drive folder or zip link, never the repo (public; screenshots are copyrighted; private reference only, never in the game); the machine dedupes, clusters by look (DINOv2), measures palette, light, saturation, grit and value per cluster, picks the heads (about 50 for 20,000); the chat LOOKS at every head and writes what it teaches; the bible's picture page carries the heads with the count behind each; a TOP subfolder of his own picks outranks the clusters; LOOK ONLY, no game in the folder becomes a reference game for design unless he names it in words. 20,000 PICTURES (10/11): his moodboard has no size limit; one Drive folder, the machine sorts, the chat looks at the cluster heads, his TOP picks outrank; look only, never in the repo; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_I_MIGHT_GIVE_YOU_20000_PICTURES_10_11_26.md. VIDEOS TOO (10/11, records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_EVERY_FRAME_OF_A_YOUTUBE_VIDEO_10_11_26.md): MP4s dropped in the folder are accepted; the coordinator's runner pulls TWO frames a second (his 10/11 call) plus one per scene change (ffmpeg select gt(scene,0.3)), dedupes, and the frames join the clusters; the pull of the video itself happens on his computer (yt-dlp / Stacher), never from the cloud, which YouTube challenges. ROUND THIRTEEN: UNTIL THE MOODBOARD, EVERYTHING IS A PLACEHOLDER, KEEP COOKING (10/11, Paolo: 'until I do this everything is a placeholder so let's keep cooking'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_UNTIL_THE_MOODBOARD_EVERYTHING_IS_A_PLACEHOLDER_KEEP_COOKING_10_11_26.md): no art reaches FINAL before his pictures are in the bible; nobody waits: the lanes build the whole pipe now (Aseprite and the scripts, the art pipe gate, the twin gate, the master rig, the parts grammar, the pack cuts, the skill file, the look-fix loop) and prove every piece of it on placeholders; the loop's logs on placeholders count as cooking; nothing is sent to his tab as a FINAL candidate until the moodboard lands, so his per-asset work is zero until then.
109. THE MAP IS BATTLE BROTHERS' SIZE, AND I PICK BATTLE BROTHERS (PAOLO 10/16, LOCKED: 'our map has to be as big as fucking Battle Brothers and that's still not the case... I don't know if we need to break the grid and have more grids... you're trying to make this as big as Pocket City 2 and Battle Brothers and you're failing, you gotta pick one and I'm choosing Battle Brothers... a larger grid or something'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_MAP_AS_BIG_AS_BATTLE_BROTHERS_PICK_ONE_10_16_26.md). (a) ONE REFERENCE FOR THE MAP: its size, its zoom range and its travel are Battle Brothers'; rule 50 (the Pocket City 2 zoom range) is SUPERSEDED for the map and Pocket City 2 goes back to the drop-in transition only (7/1); the person-on-a-bench end of the zoom is the settlement screen and the fight, never the map. (b) THE GRID GROWS OR BREAKS: the 96 by 96 valley becomes one dense middle of the whole Las Vegas region (the valley, Henderson, Boulder City, Lake Mead, the Strip, I-15 south to the dam and north toward the test site, US-95; desert, hills and shore around the city from rule 46's fifteen terrains), so a crossing takes Battle Brothers' days and a settlement is a destination; a larger grid or several grids, the lane's call. (c) THE FOUR NUMBERS ARE MEASURED (tiles across, days to cross at walking speed, settlements and locations, the zoom's near and far stops) from the library's map volume and Grok ask 26, and ours meets or beats each as the bare minimum, the shape of rule 38a's pixel floor. (d) WHO: RUN [the map at Battle Brothers' size] FIRST on its board with WORLD [the region] (the hold on WORLD lifts for this row: a rule he gave is never held); FACTIONS' bases and parties scale to the region; EYES [the map's four numbers]; PLUMBER's native map budget carries the larger grid at 60 on a phone (rule 40g).
110. 113. RUN IT LIKE THE BEST STUDIOS: FIVE LEADS, ONE PRODUCER, HIS FIFTEEN MINUTES (PAOLO 10/16, LOCKED: 'find out how the best game studios on planet Earth divide the time and resources and money towards the different departments... almost 30 chats, I cannot individually ever enter them again... I can't be having an extra part-time job... you gotta turn me up'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_RUN_IT_LIKE_A_STUDIO_AND_IT_CANNOT_LOOK_VIBE_CODED_10_16_26.md; the numbers from records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_HOW_STUDIOS_SPLIT_PEOPLE_HOURS_AND_MONEY_10_16_26.md and records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_HOW_ONE_DIRECTOR_RUNS_A_STUDIO_WITHOUT_A_SECOND_JOB_10_16_26.md). What the research found: no studio runs one director over 26 departments; managers hold 5 to 9 reports; the shape everywhere (Santa Monica, FromSoftware, Naughty Dog, Nintendo) is LEADS plus a PRODUCER, and the director sees a finished slice in one room at a milestone, never a department at a time; Insomniac's Price: 'I was the bottleneck', fixed by naming a proxy; Miyazaki scaled by sharing his logic with leads, not by more reviews; Pixar's Braintrust names the problem and never the fix; three good decisions a day is the ceiling. (a) FIVE LEADS, ONE PRODUCER. The coordinator is the producer and the dailies director: it reads every lane every sweep and he reads only it. Five lanes are LEADS and roll up the lanes under them: DIRECTION (art lead: COOK, COOK TWO, COOK THREE, COOK FOUR, PORTRAIT, ANIMATION, CHARACTER), RUN (build lead: RUN TWO, PLUMBER; MODS reports here), COMBAT (design lead: COMBAT TWO, WORLD, LIFE+CITY, ECONOMY, DYNASTY, FACTIONS, PEOPLE; TUNING reports here, QUESTS reports to WORLD), UI (presentation lead: WORDS, SOUNDS), EYES AND EARS (QA lead, the strike team). A lead's handoff block ends with ONE LINE PER LANE UNDER IT each round: what it made, the tab, and one word of three, COOKING / STUCK / FROZEN. A lead never redirects a lane's work; the board does. (b) THE HOURS SPLIT. While the build is unstable (a STOP block standing, rule 94; Cerny: still pre-production until a publishable first playable): build and pipeline 35 percent of the fleet's hours (RUN, RUN TWO, PLUMBER), art and animation 25 (DIRECTION and its seven), design and systems 20 (COMBAT and its seven), QA 10 (EYES), UI, words and sound 7, research 3 (TUNING, MODS, QUESTS). Once the demo is stable and plays on his phone: art 40, build 20, design 15, QA 12, UI words sound 10, research 3. The split is applied by the coordinator in the order and count of sessions it opens each sweep (rule 112b) and in which lanes wait when the usage is short: research first, then UI words sound, never the build while the STOP block stands. The numbers are the research page's proposal, taken as the ruling until he moves them. (c) HIS FIFTEEN MINUTES. His day: one brief (the coordinator's reply, bottom-up, eighth grade) and the VOTE tab, about fifteen minutes; the tab shows at most THREE decision groups a day and holds at most ABOUT TWENTY items waiting on him; past the cap the lanes keep cooking and the coordinator keeps culling, the tab does not grow (the keep-rate record 8/16: never grow the ballot). His week: ONE SITTING of thirty to forty-five minutes where he plays the newest build on his phone and talks; every sentence becomes a ruling or a job before the reply ends; the weekly brief ends with the FLEET SCORECARD, 26 lines grouped under the five leads, one sentence each. Once a month the coordinator writes the milestone page: where the demo stands against the ladder (slice, alpha, beta) and the one thing blocking everything. (d) WHAT NEVER REACHES HIM: work in progress; any question that starts with 'how should we'; anything technical, prioritisation or ownership (rule 8/15); anything that failed a gate; a fourth version; a text-only item. WHAT DOES: names and identity he reserved, a pillar, a reference game, an ending, a true fork with no defensible default, anything he asked to see. (e) THE FOUR SIGNALS the coordinator watches for him and prints in the weekly brief: the build stamp moved and the link plays on his phone; the VOTE tab's keep rate (under about 40 percent for two sittings means weak candidates, tighten the filter, never grow the ballot); the queue waiting on him (over twenty items or more than one bold question means the coordinator stopped shielding); fourth versions and post-kill rebuilds (zero). (f) A RULING WITHOUT ITS REASON IS UNFINISHED (Miyazaki's shared logic): every rule the coordinator writes carries his words and the why, so a lane decides the way he would without asking.
114. IT CANNOT LOOK VIBE CODED (PAOLO 10/16, LOCKED: 'anything that coming to graphics, it can't look like it's vibe coded... read everything you can on how to not look like every other vibe coded bullshit... it has to look like it was not made by you like a freaking AI guy... I'm gonna keep asking you to do rounds'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_RUN_IT_LIKE_A_STUDIO_AND_IT_CANNOT_LOOK_VIBE_CODED_10_16_26.md; round one: records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_HOW_NOT_TO_LOOK_VIBE_CODED_ROUND_ONE_10_16_26.md, 32 tells with a numeric test each, 13 master practices, the twenty-field style guide, ten gate checks ranked). What the research found: the AI look is not one defect, it is about thirty small measurable ones with one root, NOBODY DECIDED ANYTHING, so detail is everywhere, light is from nowhere, colours are from everywhere and the grid disagrees with itself. The five biggest, in order: MIXELS (two native pixel sizes in one scene; ours came from different chats at different sizes), NO SHARED PALETTE and too many colours per sprite (over 16 is a tell), NO ONE LIGHT DIRECTION across the sprites of a scene, STRAIGHT DARKENING with no hue shift in the ramps (the signature of a shade() function), and THE SAME DETAIL EVERYWHERE with no rest area and no focal point. (a) THE STYLE GUIDE IS LAW. DIRECTION writes the pixel-art style guide with the twenty fields of the research page's Section C filled with REAL NUMBERS (one native pixel size and integer display scale; the master palette file with roles and 4-to-5-step ramps hue-shifting at least 8 degrees; a colour cap per asset class; one key light for every asset; three values minimum, shadows never black; the outline rule per class; AA and dither rules; proportions and one silhouette feature per enemy class; a detail budget per class with a flat rest region; two variants per base tile and no run over four; the contact line under every standing thing; UI with the project's pixel font, no gradients, no blur, no glow, radius 0 or 1, no system fonts; the tie-breaker: readability at 1x over everything, palette over detail, silhouette over colour; a do-and-don't pair per field; the review procedure) as a data file the gates read, inside the analog horror bible's folder. Every field is a gate (rule: a law without a machine gate is not enforced). Until the file exists, the five biggest tells are the review, by hand, on every new sheet. (b) THE TEN GATES. PLUMBER builds Section D's ten checks as the NOT VIBE CODED family in the suite, in the research page's order (pixel size, palette and colour count, light direction, hue shift, detail distribution, silhouette separation, three-value read, clean lines, repetition and variation, UI defaults), each a pure image or data-file test over the PNGs a VOTE sheet carries and over the demo's screenshots; every VOTE sheet carries its report; a sheet that fails the first five never reaches the tab (the coordinator culls it, rule 113d). (c) EVERY COOK, FROM THIS ROUND: a sheet names its pixel size, its palette file and its light direction in its caption; hero assets (the player, a boss, the house on screen) are hand-finished after the pipe; a tile ships with its two variants; nothing is drawn by darkening. The reference check compares art to the world; these gates compare art to itself, the half that was missing. (d) ROUNDS CONTINUE. Each time he asks, the coordinator runs the next research round on a new angle (round two's first candidates: how Dead Cells' 3D-to-pixel pipe is hand-finished so it reads drawn; how Blasphemous and Eastward budgeted detail; how a 2D studio runs art QA with contact sheets at 1x), numbered, cited, and folded into the style guide's numbers and the gates, never into a reply only. (e) Rule 108 stands: nothing is FINAL before his moodboard; these gates make the candidates honest, they do not make them final.
115. THE RIG'S LOOK IS THE LOOK (PAOLO 10/17, LOCKED; the thirteenth votes and his words: 'Holy shit you're making like 3-D looking 2-D sprites. I think we have to do that for the rest of the game... the first thing I've been impressed with visual wise in a long time'; 'you made a truck and a robot and I fell in love, this analog 3-D, HBO early kids show kind of vibe, I love that art direction... the character models compared to the terrain and the buildings look like dogshit... I don't know if we have to remake all the assets character model wise... whatever is easy for you to keep up the flow and continue to make shit like that'; 'for everything to start looking better it has to come from the same source'; 'just make sure everything's looking the same'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_NEVER_ASK_ME_TO_APPROVE_AGAIN_AND_THE_CLAY_RIG_IS_THE_LOOK_10_17_26.md). (a) THE METHOD IS FINAL: every character, beast, vehicle and prop is MODELLED AT THE SOURCE and rendered to pixels through DIRECTION's master rig, the clay-and-tape way the robot and the truck were made, so everything comes from one source and looks the same. The old roads for these are DEAD: the 2D parts grammar (his 10/17 NO twice: 'this isn't that', 'one of the worst cooks'), cutting flat garments into pieces for the rig (his NO: 'glitchy and fucked up'), hand-drawn eight-direction sprites. (b) WHAT STAYS ON THE PACKS: the ground (his YES on the curb, the crossing, the 47 corners, the recolour; his NO on the Vegas block is a composition NO, not a method NO) and, until DIRECTION rules from the two research pages, the buildings (his YES on the straight-roof family, the corner shop, the motel; his note: roofs more tan, never bright medieval orange or metal blue). (c) THE CHARACTER MODELS ARE REMADE through the rig: the player's body and the thirteen first (CHARACTER models the runway clothes ON the rig, never cut from flat art), then the beasts (ANIMATION; the dire wolf redone, his NO: the grey one is the ugliest, the fox is better), then the faces (PORTRAIT renders the HD face from the same model), then the enemy tiers (COOK THREE; a trenchcoat must read as a trenchcoat, his NO). The old flat sprites stay in the game until each replacement passes the VOTE tab; assets are still candidates one by one (rule 108 stands for assets; the METHOD no longer waits on the moodboard). (d) THE LOOK BIBLE: DIRECTION owns it from two research pages, records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_THE_TOP_TEN_ANALOG_HORROR_GAMES_WHAT_THEIR_LOOK_IS_MADE_OF_10_17_26.md (a GENRE STUDY; no game in it becomes a reference game; nothing in it is copied) and records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_THE_CREEPY_CLAYMATION_KIDS_SHOW_LOOK_AND_HOW_A_RIG_GETS_IT_10_17_26.md (the shows are candidates until he names them); the rig's recipe (frame stepping, no motion blur, clay shading, one hard light, the analog pass, the palette) becomes rows of the style guide (rule 114a) so the gates read it. (e) RESEARCH ROUNDS CONTINUE on his ask (rule 114d). (f) His smaller words from the same votes, each a job: the shadow line behind the main character (ANIMATION); the ragdoll choppy and too slow (ANIMATION); the blue or orange outline around people in the lit fight (COMBAT); the map 'really fat' and the view changes with the orientation (COMBAT, rule 104a's plain form); the map must look good on the phone AND on a laptop, where widescreen is a more zoomed-out phone view (RUN); too many birds and insects for a desert city (SOUNDS); the recap voice unusable (SOUNDS); the title's hiss too loud and the music behind it bad (SOUNDS); a whole app on the phone to integrate (UI); no more cards with quests, make the quest, the pixels and the sound (QUESTS, WORLD, RUN TWO; the law A QUEST IS PEOPLE, PLACES AND THINGS stands); the fifty perk names as a list is a NO (COMBAT: names come from a mouth, in play). (g) THE DEMO WEARS THE RIG (PAOLO 10/18: 'is the demo changing, I liked the robot that got made type shit'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_KEEP_GOING_TWO_HOURS_IS_THE_DEMO_CHANGING_10_18_26.md): the look he liked reaches the DEMO, not only the tab; the first rig-made things that pass the VOTE tab ride RUN's next cut (the party's people and the first beast first); until a replacement passes, the demo keeps the old sprite; RUN [the demo wears the rig]. ROUND TWO of rule 114's research is the rig itself (how 3D-to-pixel studios keep a render from reading as a render; the hand-finish; the source settings; ten gate checks): records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_HOW_NOT_TO_LOOK_VIBE_CODED_ROUND_TWO_THE_RIG_10_18_26.md, folded into DIRECTION's look bible when it lands. (h) THE FIRST STAR (PAOLO 10/18, the fourteenth votes, on PORTRAIT's poacher face built as a 3D head on the body's own model: 'You might change the game with this one big star event... this is the first star I've handed out'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_FIRST_STAR_AND_EASIER_THAN_BATTLE_BROTHERS_10_18_26.md): the face from the same model is the method for EVERY face, and it replaces the old portraits on the screens he named first (RUN TWO's crew and scavenge screens: 'the portrait sucks', 'the portrait is ass'). AMENDED 10/18 (his note on RUN TWO's starred-faces card: 'I liked it when it was the portrait, not when you zoom in on the creepy model's face... it has to be made fresh portrait'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_A_FRESH_PORTRAIT_NEVER_A_ZOOM_ON_THE_MODEL_10_18_26.md): A FRESH PORTRAIT, NEVER A ZOOM ON THE MODEL: the face is the head modelled on the body's own model and rendered for the portrait with its own camera, framing and light; a crop or zoom of a body sprite or render is never a portrait, not even as a stopgap; PORTRAIT makes the fresh one before a screen ships. AMENDED (d) 10/18 (HE NAMED CRASHBOX; Grok 160 and 159 in the Grok folder, brought onto main 10/18; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_LOOK_AGAIN_GROKS_MUSIC_AND_CRASHBOX_ARE_IN_10_18_26.md): the creepy HBO claymation kids' show is CRASHBOX (HBO Family, 1999 to 2000, Cuppa Coffee Studios): stop-motion clay with puppets and cutouts inside a handmade broken game computer, rusty tin robots, clay that still looks like clay, faces simple and a little wrong, held poses not smooth motion, nothing glows. It is the look bible's reference (art only, DIRECTION); Moral Orel is out by his word; the other shows Grok listed stay candidates.
116. THE FLEET RUNS ON WHATEVER MODEL HAS USAGE, AND THE COORDINATOR SWITCHES IT (PAOLO 10/18, LOCKED: 'the Fable 5 limit was reached bro, I'm not changing them one by one man, u do it'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_FABLE_LIMIT_WAS_REACHED_YOU_DO_IT_10_18_26.md). (a) A lane session that fails on one model's usage limit is archived and reopened on the next model that has usage by the coordinator, the same sweep, its first message telling it to resume its CLAIMED row; he never switches a chat's model. (b) Only the coordinator's own chat is switched by him, and only when it is the one at the limit. (c) The hourly routine stops only when EVERY model reports a limit, or on his word (amends 111(c) and 112(c)). (d) Claim before work (rule 5) and commit small: a session that dies mid-round loses its uncommitted work, never its job. Applied 10/18 03:26 to 03:55 UTC: all 23 lanes moved from Fable to Opus 5.5. AMENDED 10/18 (PAOLO: 'Can you make sure they run on Opus 5.5 Extra, let's not use the extra usage right now'): every lane opens on Opus 5.5 at the Extra effort (.claude/settings.json effortLevel xhigh, capped there by maxEffortLevel so nothing runs at Max); NO EXTRA USAGE: a lane that hits the usage cap stops and waits for the reset, it never runs on extra (paid) usage; the coordinator reads each session's overage flag every sweep and stops any lane that shows it.
117. EASIER THAN BATTLE BROTHERS (PAOLO 10/18, LOCKED, on TUNING's numbers card: 'I want you to be easier than Battle Brothers... bringing Battle Brothers into this fun, like Nintendo simplified way kind of vibes, like minimalist vibes... if there's a lot to do, let's just make the people feel that they're successfully doing it, really good vibes'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_FIRST_STAR_AND_EASIER_THAN_BATTLE_BROTHERS_10_18_26.md). Battle Brothers is the model for HOW a system works (rule 41), never for how hard it is. (a) Every felt number starts EASIER than Battle Brothers' and the difficulty sliders go up from there; its default sits at our hard end. (b) Nintendo-simple and minimalist on the screen: fewer numbers shown, fewer buttons, one clear next thing; the depth (formation and gear, rule 37) lives under the surface. (c) The player feels successful: every good choice gets a visible and audible win; a busy screen shows progress, never a to-do list. (d) His trade of realism for fun, made (the realism-first law gives him the call). TUNING writes it into the one table (research only); COMBAT, RUN TWO and UI build to it; a design page that sets a number harder than Battle Brothers' without his word is a NO before he sees it. (e) A TUNING NUMBER IS A GRID, NEVER ONE AVERAGE (PAOLO 10/18: 'how are you even testing these fights... against animals, against different group sizes, one person, three, six, up to 14... a 12-man Lone Wolf squad can go up to 36 or 40 enemies... we don't even have all the equipment in the game... what are you even testing?'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_WHAT_ARE_YOU_EVEN_TESTING_A_TUNING_NUMBER_IS_A_GRID_10_18_26.md): the fight bench covers the company at 1, 3, 6, 12 and 14, the enemy from a few to 36 to 40, human bands and every beast that exists, early, middle and late gear; one row per cell, the worst cells first; every number DRAFT until the gear is coordinated; no VOTE card shows one average as the game's difficulty.
118. THE COORDINATOR SAYS 'IN THE VOTE TAB' ONLY FOR A CARD ON HIS FIRST SCREEN (PAOLO 10/18, LOCKED: 'A lot of the votes you saying were on a card visible we're not visible for me'; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_CARDS_YOU_NAMED_WERE_NOT_ON_MY_SCREEN_10_18_26.md).
